brief.title: Keep the Wick
brief.premise: A new lamplighter in a moor parish learns that the parish's wall lanterns must never all go dark on the same night, and that last winter's ledger of lit nights has a page cut out.
constraints: The parish is remote and pre-industrial; no firearms or engines.

world.name: The Lantern Parish
world.description: A remote moor parish whose boundary wall carries a line of lanterns that must never all go dark on one night, for the bog walks when the light fails.

locations.name: The Lantern Wall
locations.description: The parish boundary wall, niched with lamps that are lit each dusk without fail.

locations.name: The Moot Kirk
locations.description: The parish church where the ledger of lit nights is kept and the council sits.

locations.name: The Bog Hollow
locations.description: The peat cuttings below the moor where lights drown and voices carry wrong.

locations.name: The Keeper's Croft
locations.description: The lamplighter's cottage at the wall's foot, with its oil store and wick bench.

factions.name: The Lamp Wardens
factions.description: The guild that keeps the wall, cuts the wicks and owes the parish its lit nights.

factions.name: The Moot Council
factions.description: The parish council that keeps the ledger and calls in the oil tithe.

factions.name: The Turf-Cutters
factions.description: The families who cut peat in the bog and owe oil to the wall.

rules.statement: Never may all the lanterns go dark on the same night; at least one wick must burn on the wall.
Every lit night is entered in the ledger at the Moot Kirk; an unentered night did not happen.
No lantern may be carried past the bog line after dusk.
Every hearth owes a measure of oil to the wall; unpaid tithes are called in at midwinter.

history.name: The Dark Winter
history.description: In the parish's first year, every lamp failed on one night and half the hearths were empty by spring.

history.name: The First Wick
history.description: The wall was raised and the lantern rite begun so no night would ever be wholly dark again.

history.name: The Missing Page
history.description: A page was cut from the ledger of lit nights, and no warden will say which night it held.

conflicts.name: The Missing Night
conflicts.description: The cut page may hide a night the wall went dark, and the council and wardens each blame the other for the silence.

conflicts.name: The Oil Shortfall
conflicts.description: The turf-cutters owe oil and say the wardens over-count the call-in, while the wall burns short.

characters.name: Wenna Crowe
characters.description: The new lamplighter, apprenticed into the wardens from outside the parish, who keeps the wick bench and asks questions the parish has stopped asking.
characters.motivation: To learn what the missing page hid before midwinter tests the wall again.
characters.goal: Find the truth of the dark night and keep every lantern lit through the winter.
characters.flaw: She needs proof before she will fear anything, and the bog does not give proof.
characters.internal_conflict: The rite she keeps is either sacred or superstition, and the missing page could say which.
characters.external_conflict: The council cut the page to keep the parish calm, and a calm parish is one that stops feeding the wall.

abilities.name: Wick-craft
abilities.description: Keeps a flame alive in moor wind and driving wet better than any warden before her.

characters.arc: Wenna learns that the missing page was cut to hide not the dark, but what the parish did about it.

characters.name: Reeve Toll
characters.description: The parish reeve who cut the page from the ledger and has kept the parish's peace ever since.
characters.motivation: To keep the parish orderly and fed, whatever it takes not to know.
characters.goal: Keep the dark night buried through one more midwinter.
characters.flaw: He believes an orderly lie keeps more hearths lit than the truth.
characters.internal_conflict: He cut the page to save the parish, and cannot forgive himself for how well it worked.
characters.external_conflict: Wenna's questions threaten the silence that has kept the tithes coming.

abilities.name: Council writ
abilities.description: Writes and wields parish orders with a speed that outruns every question.

characters.arc: Toll's page is read back to him in front of the moot he deceived to save.

characters.name: Lob Ather
characters.description: A turf-cutter who was out past the bog line on the missing night and saw the wall go dark.
characters.motivation: To protect his family from the oil call-in and from what he saw.
characters.goal: Keep his hearth's oil until spring without betraying what he witnessed.
characters.flaw: Fear makes him lie first and tell the truth last.
characters.internal_conflict: His silence keeps his family safe and the parish blind.
characters.external_conflict: The reeve's writ can seize his oil, and the bog takes stragglers.

abilities.name: Bog-reading
abilities.description: Reads the bog's sounds and lights and tells which are only weather.

characters.arc: Lob says aloud, once, what he saw, and the parish changes.

relationships.description: Lob alone can tell Wenna what the missing page held.
relationships.conflict: His testimony costs him the council's mercy.

relationships.description: Wenna's questions undo the silence Toll cut the page to keep.
relationships.conflict: Each believes their way is the only thing holding back the dark.

evidence_summary: The world, cast and storyboard satisfy the brief's lantern-keeping folk-horror setting; deterministic validators are clean and there are no blocking defects.
